s1.syndrome_frame: Congenital vascular and soft tissue anomalies with overgrowth and malformations
salient_findings: Multiple soft masses on the anterior upper chest, abdomen, and right arm
Large port-wine–colored capillary malformation on the trunk
Hypertrophy of the left thigh, overgrowth of both feet, and syndactyly of the toes
key_facts: 20-month-old girl with congenital soft-tissue masses and cutaneous vascular lesions
Multiple soft masses on the anterior upper chest, abdomen, and right arm since birth
Large port-wine–colored capillary malformation partially involving the trunk
Hypertrophy of the left thigh
Overgrowth of both feet
Syndactyly of the second and third toes on the right
Dilated, tortuous veins over the chest and left leg
No facial dysmorphism
No cardiac murmur
No organomegaly
Full muscle strength
Intact reflexes
Normal developmental milestones and growth parameters
Born by cesarean delivery to a nonconsanguineous couple
Pregnancy notable for fetal malformations
Two older siblings healthy
Skeletal survey demonstrated fused toes and soft-tissue hypertrophy
MRI revealed extensive cystic, septated, high–T2-signal masses consistent with lymphangiomas
Liver, kidneys, and pancreas appeared normal aside from hemangiomas

shortlist.label: Klippel-Trenaunay-Weber syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by congenital vascular malformations, soft tissue hypertrophy, and limb overgrowth, matching key clinical features

shortlist.label: Parkes Weber syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Involves capillary malformations, soft tissue and skeletal hypertrophy, and arteriovenous fistulas, consistent with patient's presentation

shortlist.label: CLOVES syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Features congenital lipomatous overgrowth, vascular malformations, and epidermal nevi, aligning with patient's congenital soft-tissue masses and cutaneous vascular lesions

shortlist.label: Proteus syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by an overgrowth of skin, bones, and organs, with a high risk of vascular malformations, which could explain the patient's complex clinical picture

shortlist.label: Blue rubber bleb nevus syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Involves multiple venous malformations and can present with soft tissue hypertrophy, although less typical, it remains a plausible diagnosis given the patient's vascular and soft tissue anomalies

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of congenital soft-tissue masses, cutaneous vascular lesions, port-wine stain, hypertrophy of the left thigh, and overgrowth of both feet are consistent with Klippel-Trenaunay-Weber syndrome, which is characterized by a triad of port-wine stains, varicose veins or malformations, and bony and soft tissue hypertrophy.

rejected.label: Parkes Weber syndrome
rejected.why: While similar to Klippel-Trenaunay-Weber syndrome, Parkes Weber syndrome typically involves arteriovenous malformations, which are not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: CLOVES syndrome
rejected.why: CLOVES syndrome involves congenital lipomatous overgrowth, vascular malformations, epidermal nevi, and skeletal anomalies, but the patient's presentation does not specifically mention lipomatous overgrowth or epidermal nevi.

rejected.label: Proteus syndrome
rejected.why: Proteus syndrome is characterized by an overgrowth of multiple tissues, but the patient's normal developmental milestones and growth parameters do not support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Blue rubber bleb nevus syndrome
rejected.why: This syndrome involves multiple venous malformations, but the patient's presentation of lymphangiomas and port-wine stains is more consistent with Klippel-Trenaunay-Weber syndrome.
